Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:78: And so one who conceals his good deeds from people has, as his reward, that he be hidden from the masters of judgment - for the Holy One, blessed be He, covers him with the garment of Chesed, called "Eloah," so that the masters of judgment not recognize him - and this is alluded to in the verse (Job 3:23), "to a man whose way is hidden, whom Eloah has hedged in" - and it is known that the name "Eloah" is the garment for the soul, as it is written (ibid. 29:2), "as in the days when Eloah watched over me," and as explained in the Sabba (Parashat Mishpatim, page 96b), on the verse (Exodus 21:8), "he shall have no power to sell her to a foreign people, seeing he has dealt deceitfully with her."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:79: And one who publicizes that he is fasting is punished - and so the Tashbetz wrote (Katan, section 111): it is forbidden to publicize to others that one is fasting - and he brought from the Yerushalmi (Chagigah, chapter 2, halachah 2), in these words: Rabbi Yosi bar Chanina said, the hinge of the gate of Gehinnom is fixed in his ear. They said to him, why is this so? He said to them, because she [a certain woman] would fast and publicize it - and some say she would fast one day and it would harm her for two - to this point, relevant here. And the intent of the fixed hinge is explained as being so that the hole go from ear to ear.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:80: Also, a great repair for the penitent is that he strive to observe Shabbat's entry properly, and in the observance of Shabbat itself - for all the days nurse from the day of Shabbat, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Noach, page 75b), and we elaborated in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 7.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:81: And I saw fit, to complete this chapter, to copy things that lengthen days, explained (Ta'anit 20b) concerning fasts, that his students asked Rabbi Ze'ira - and some say Rav Adda bar Ahavah - to what do you attribute your length of days? He said to them: in all my days I was never impatient within my house, nor did I walk ahead of one greater than myself, nor did I contemplate [Torah thoughts] in filthy alleyways, nor did I walk four cubits without Torah and without tefillin, nor did I sleep in the study hall, neither a fixed sleep nor a passing nap, nor did I rejoice at my fellow's mishap, nor did I call my fellow by his nickname - and some say, by his family's nickname - to this point. And Rashi, peace be upon him, explained "by his nickname" as a name people give him, such as an added name; "by his family's nickname," like the family nicknames in Gittin up to ten generations (Gittin 88a) - and the Tosafot explained (Ta'anit 20b, s.v. "be-chanikhto") as up to ten [generations], such as Rabbi Avraham Ibn Ezra, whose whole family was called this way - and this is specifically for disparagement, but for praise it is permitted - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:82: And to these deeds of Rav Adda bar Ahavah, they added more in the Yerushalmi (Ta'anit, chapter 3, halachah 11), in these words: the Sages sent and said to him, what good deeds do you have? He said to them: in all my days, no person ever preceded me to the synagogue; I never left anyone in the synagogue and went out [before them]; I never walked four cubits without Torah; I never mentioned words of Torah in a filthy place; I never spread out and slept a fixed sleep; I never took large steps among my companions; I never gave a [derogatory] nickname to my fellow; I never rejoiced at my fellow's mishap; I never let my fellow's curse come upon my bed [i.e., went to sleep angry]; I never walked in the marketplace near someone who owed me money; in all my days I was never impatient within my house - to fulfill what is said (Psalms 101:2), "I will walk within my house with a perfect heart" - to this point. There are further several things for length of days, stated in Tractate Megillah (28a) and copied in Chapter "Derech Eretz."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:83: Also, it is fitting to be careful with the attribute of truth, whose virtue is length of days, as explained in the Gate of Holiness. Also, when the penitent is weak in his fast, especially if he is a Torah scholar and cannot delve deeply, he should read, during those hours, matters of aggadah that draw the heart, and not sit idle, for one who sits idle from words of Torah is called a scoffer. And the pious Rabbi Yosef Yavetz, peace be upon him, wrote, on the mishnah of "sleeping in the morning," and so on (Avot, chapter 3, mishnah 10), in these words: and Ibn Ezra, of blessed memory, wrote, there is a way to relieve a weakened soul with a difficult halachah - the God-fearing one shall fulfill all views, and seek, for those hours, easy matters to understand, so that his discourse not become a cause to distract him from the world and lose what he gained from deep study - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:84: And when the penitent strives to fulfill all these things, heaven will assist him, without doubt.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:1: This chapter will explain several matters in which a person stumbles, which are transgressions that people trample underfoot, and the penitent must be careful of them, so that his repentance be accepted.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:2: The first thing one must be careful of is neglecting Torah, for the punishment for neglecting words of Torah is great, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, expounded in the Yerushalmi (Chagigah, chapter 1, halachah 7), on the verse (Jeremiah 9:12), "and the LORD said, because they have forsaken My Torah" - Rabbi Huna and Rabbi Yirmiyah in the name of Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak: we find that the Holy One, blessed be He, forgave idolatry, forbidden relations, and bloodshed, but did not forgive the rejection of Torah. "Why has the land perished" - because of idolatry, forbidden relations, bloodshed - it is not written here, but rather "because they have forsaken My Torah." Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said, it is written, "and Me they have forsaken" - a mere forsaking; but had they kept My Torah, perhaps the light within it would have drawn them near to Me. Rav Huna said, study Torah even not for its own sake, for since you occupy yourself with it, you will come to do it for its own sake - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:3: Further, in Tanchuma (Parashat Re'eh, section 1), in these words: this is what Scripture says (Jeremiah 21:8), "and to this people you shall say, thus says the LORD: behold, I set before you the way of life and the way of death," and it is written (Psalms 78:1), "give ear, O my people, to my Torah; incline your ears to the words of my mouth," and it is written (Deuteronomy 4:9), "only take heed to yourself, and keep your soul diligently," and so on, and it is written (ibid. 4:10), "the day that you stood" - to teach you that whoever neglects Torah is as though he denies the Holy One, blessed be He, for He gave the Torah to Israel only that they occupy themselves with it day and night, and it is written (Joshua 1:8), "and you shall meditate on it day and night," and so on, and it is written (Psalms 1:2), "but his delight is in the Torah of the LORD," and so on. And whoever occupies himself with Torah and fulfills it is as though he received it at Sinai - and therefore it is written (Deuteronomy 4:9-10), "and you shall teach them to your children and your children's children, the day that you stood" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:4: And one who could occupy himself with Torah and does not, is included in "he has despised the word of the LORD" (Numbers 15:31), as we say in Sanhedrin (99a) on the verse "for he has despised the word of the LORD": Rabbi Natan says, this is anyone who does not pay attention to the Mishnah. Rabbi Nechemyah says, anyone who could occupy himself with Torah and does not - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:5: And in the Yalkut on the Prophets (Yalkut Yehoshua, page 2, section 7), it says in Tanna D'Vei Eliyahu: "prepare provisions for yourselves" (Joshua 1:11) - and did they need provisions there? Were they not eating manna, which they gathered every morning? Rather, he said this to them: repent, so that you enter the land and eat of the produce of the land, as it is said (Joshua 5:12), "and the manna ceased on the next day." An angel went forth to destroy the whole world - he said, the manna has ceased, and the Torah has ceased [being studied], as it is said (Joshua 5:13), "and it came to pass, when Joshua was by Jericho," and so on - he said to him, and Joshua, are you wearing shoes, and you are not observing mourning for Israel, that the manna has ceased and the Torah has ceased? [Remove] the shoe from your foot. Therefore I would say, happy is the person who increases his sitting [in study] and his effort, and diminishes his commerce, sitting and meditating on words of Torah every single day always - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:6: And in Eruvin (63a) they said concerning this matter, "and he said, no, but I am captain of the host of the LORD" (Joshua 5:14) - he said to him, yesterday evening you neglected the daily evening offering; now you have neglected Torah study. And he said to him, for which of these have you come? He said to him, I have come now. Immediately, "and Joshua lodged that night in the midst of the valley" - Rabbi Yochanan said, this teaches that he lodged in the depths of halachah, and so on. And further there, Rav Shmuel bar Abba said in the name of Rav, Torah study is greater than the offering of the daily sacrifices, as it is said, "I have come now" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:7: And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 52, page 87a) they said, in these words: woe to the people who do not strive in Torah, who are called dry wood, destined to be burned in the fire of Gehinnom - and it is not for nothing that the masters of the Mishnah said, "they toil and inherit Gehinnom" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:8: And the reason for all this is that the Torah is bound to His Name, and the Torah guides a person to perform the commandments, and the commandments too are bound to His Name - it follows that one who does not occupy himself with Torah is as though he denies the Holy One, blessed be He, and this is "he has despised the word of the LORD" - and therefore Gehinnom rules over him, as it is said (Deuteronomy 31:17), "is it not because our God is not among us that these evils have found us," as explained above in the previous chapter.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:9: And besides the Torah being a guide to performing the commandments, through occupation with it one also attains knowledge of the secret of the supernal divinity - for this was His intent, blessed be He, in writing the Torah for us with these open and closed passages, and several extra and missing letters, because it alludes to the measure of the supernal stature - and therefore, if even one letter is missing, it is disqualified, because it is not in the supernal image.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:10: As is proven in the Zohar (Parashat Acharei Mot, page 71a), in these words: we have learned, Rabbi Yehuda said: one day Rabbi Chizkiyah and Rabbi Yesa were walking on the road; they happened upon Gush Chalav, and it was in ruins; they sat near a burial place, and Rabbi Yesa had in his hand a Torah scroll fragment that had been torn. While they sat, a certain grave stirred before them and cried, "woe, woe, for the world is found in distress; is Torah being revealed here, or living beings [scholars] have come to mock us, or bring us shame with their Torah?" Rabbi Chizkiyah and Rabbi Yesa trembled; Rabbi Chizkiyah said, who are you? He said to him, I am dead, and I was aroused at the sight of a Torah scroll - for once the world sat in distress, and living beings came here to arouse us with a Torah scroll; and I and my companions preceded my sleeping companions [in death]. When they joined in the Garden of Eden with the spirits of the righteous, that Torah scroll that these living ones brought before us was found to be invalid, falsifying the King's Name, for there was an extra vav found in this verse (Leviticus 11:3), "that has cloven hooves [u-shosa'at shesa parsot]" - and they said, since they falsified the King's Name, we shall not return to them, and they drove me and my companions out of the heavenly academy at that hour - to this point. And the rest of the account is not relevant to our subject.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:11: And so he says in the Zohar (Parashat Vayechi, page 225a): but I found one remedy in the world, and only one - in that place where those who labor in Torah are found, and among them a Torah scroll is found that is not falsified - when this one takes it out, the upper and lower ones are aroused because of it, and all the more so if the holy Name is written properly - and we have thus learned this matter - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:12: And this is the essence of the completeness in occupation with Torah - to know one's Owner and cleave to Him, and so on. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained this exposition in [the Zohar on] Song of Songs (Zohar Chadash, page 70b), in these words: "if you do not know, O fairest among women" (Song of Songs 1:8) - it is written (Deuteronomy 4:39), "know this day, and consider it in your heart, that the LORD, He is God" - happy are all who strive in Torah, to know the wisdom of their Master, and they know and gaze into supernal secrets - for when a person departs this world with this, all the judgments of the world depart from him, and moreover, thirteen gates of the secrets of pure balsam are opened for him, in which the secrets of supernal wisdom depend; and moreover, the Holy One, blessed be He, engraves him on that royal robe on which all forms are engraved, both in this world and in the World to Come, and the Holy One, blessed be He, delights in him in the Garden of Eden, and he inherits two worlds, this world and the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:13: The wisdom a person needs, to know and gaze at everything through the secret of his Master, is one, to know and gaze at the secret of his Master; and one, to know his own body, and to recognize who he is, how he was created, from where he comes and to where he goes, and how the repair of the body is repaired, and how he is destined to enter judgment before the King of all; and one, to know and gaze at the secrets of his soul - what is that soul within him, and from where does it come, and for what purpose does it come into this body, a putrid drop, here today and tomorrow in the grave; and one, to gaze at this world he is in, and for what it is repaired, and afterward at the secrets of the world above, to know his Master - and all this a person contemplates within the secrets of the Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:14: Come and see, whoever goes to that world without knowledge, even if he has many deeds, they take him out of all the gates of that world - go and see what is said there: tell me the secrets of wisdom that I did not know and did not learn until now, so that I not be ashamed among those supernal levels I am entering, for until now I did not gaze upon them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:15: Come and see what is written, "if you do not know, O fairest one" - if you come without knowledge, and did not gaze at wisdom before entering, and did not know the secrets of the supernal world, "go your way" - you cannot enter here without knowledge - to this point, relevant here. And the rest of the verse is explained there along the lines mentioned.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:16: And through this may be understood what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in Tanchuma, that the verse (Jeremiah 9:23), "but let him who boasts boast in this, that he understands and knows Me" is said of the Torah, in these words: and how does a person boast in this world? In the crown of Torah, which enriches him and gives him life in this world and the World to Come, as it is said (Proverbs 3:16), "length of days is in her right hand; in her left hand are riches and honor" - and it gives him strength that shall never cease, as it is said (Isaiah 40:31), "but those who wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength" - to this point. And this is because the Torah is called "zot," as he says (Deuteronomy 4:44), "and this [ve-zot] is the Torah that Moses set." And the conclusion of the verse, "he understands and knows [Me]" - for through the Torah we know Him, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:17: And because "the beginning of strife is like letting out water" (Proverbs 17:14), as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Kiddushin 40b), that the first thing a person is judged on is whether he occupied himself with Torah - therefore the beginning of repentance must be occupation with Torah, for study leads to deed. And therefore we say in prayer, "return us, our Father, to Your Torah," and afterward, "and bring us near to Your service."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:18: And when he occupies himself with Torah for its own sake - which is to study and to do, as explained in the Introduction to this book - the secrets of the Torah shall be revealed to him, as Rabbi Meir said (Avot, chapter 6, mishnah 1): whoever occupies himself with Torah for its own sake merits many things, and so on, and the secrets of the Torah are revealed to him, and he becomes like an ever-strengthening spring. And so too through repentance, as it is written (Proverbs 1:23), "return at my reproof; behold, I will pour out my spirit to you, I will make known my words to you."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:19: Further, he should examine whether he has transgressed one of the twenty-four things for which one is excommunicated, which Rambam wrote in the Laws of Torah Study, and these are: 1) one who disgraces a Sage, even after his death; 2) one who disgraces an agent of the court; 3) one who calls his fellow "slave"; 4) one who belittles even one matter of the words of the Scribes, needless to say the words of the Torah; 5) one whom the court has summoned and set a time for, and he did not come; 6) one who does not accept the judgment upon himself - they excommunicate him until he pays; 7) one who has in his possession something harmful, such as a vicious dog or a rickety ladder - they excommunicate him until he removes the hazard; 8) one who sells his land to a gentile - they excommunicate him until he accepts upon himself any coercion that comes from the gentile against his Israelite neighbor who owns the adjoining land; 9) one who testifies against a fellow Jew in gentile courts and thereby extracts money from him unlawfully through his testimony - they excommunicate him until he repays; 10) a slaughterer who does not separate the priestly gifts and give them to a priest - they excommunicate him until he gives them; 11) one who desecrates the second day of festivals observed in the Diaspora, even though it is [only] a custom; 12) one who performs labor on the eve of Passover after midday; 13) one who mentions the Name of Heaven in vain or in a frivolous oath, in idle talk; 14) one who causes the multitude to eat consecrated food outside [the Temple precincts]; 15) one who causes the multitude to profane the Name; 16) one who calculates years and fixes months outside the Land of Israel; 17) one who causes the blind to stumble; 18) one who prevents the multitude from performing a commandment; 19) a slaughterer from whose hand a torn animal has emerged [repeatedly]; 20) a slaughterer who did not show his knife for inspection to a Sage; 21) one who causes himself an erection intentionally; 22) one who divorced his wife and then formed a partnership or business dealings with her that bring them to interact with one another - when both come to judgment, they are excommunicated; 23) a Sage of bad reputation; 24) one who excommunicates someone who does not deserve excommunication.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:20: And they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Pekudei, page 249b), that in the Heichal of Nogah there are four angels with several bands who excommunicate those who defile their mouths, and likewise all those whose sins require rebuke - ten heralds go forth every day and proclaim in all those firmaments and in all those hosts and camps: beware of so-and-so, who is under rebuke; the rebuke is such-and-such a sin so-and-so did, until he returns before his Master - may the Merciful One save us! When he returns from that sin, these forty gather and release him, and then they proclaim, so-and-so's rebuke is released - from here on his prayer enters; and until he returns, he is under rebuke above and below, and his Master's protection is removed from him, and even at night his soul is under rebuke, for all the gates of heaven are closed to it, and it does not ascend, and they push it away outside - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:21: Therefore one must examine his deeds to see whether he has sinned in one of these matters - especially if he caused himself an erection intentionally, which is a common thing among young men who have not yet married - he must accept rebuke upon himself, and sit on the ground as one excommunicated, and in a wrapped garment - and so we find David accepted rebuke upon himself, as explained above (chapter 3), and so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained in Midrash Yalkut (Samuel, section 95, page 15d, and also Midrash Tadshe there).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:22: Further, if he sinned with his limbs, he should perform commandments with them - and this matter is explained in Midrash Yalkut (Judges, remez 42): all the tribes appointed judges and kings, but the tribe of Simeon, because it sinned with sexual immorality, appointed neither judge nor king. And it further says: therefore the covenant of circumcision was placed on the sexual organ, so that fear of the Omnipresent restrain from committing that sin. For every sensation, the Holy One, blessed be He, gave a Torah of what to do and what not to do. For the heart - "and you shall not go about after your own heart and after your own eyes" (Numbers 15:39). For the ears - "you shall not raise a false report" (Exodus 23:1). For the mouth - "you shall not eat any abominable thing" (Deuteronomy 14:3). For the tongue - "you shall not take the name of the LORD [in vain]" (Exodus 20:7), "you shall not swear falsely" (Leviticus 19:12), "you shall not lie" (Leviticus 19:11). For the hands - "put not your hand with the wicked" (Exodus 23:1). For forbidden relations - "you shall not commit adultery" (Exodus 20:13), "you shall not commit harlotry." For the feet - "you shall not go after other gods" (ibid. 20:3) - all these are negative commandments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:23: And what to do - it teaches, for the heart - "and you shall place these My words upon your heart" (Deuteronomy 11:18). For the eyes - "lest you forget the things which your eyes have seen" (ibid. 4:9). For the ears - "Hear, O Israel, the statutes" (ibid. 5:1). For the tongue - "and you shall teach them diligently to your children" (ibid. 6:7). For the hands - "you shall surely open your hand" (ibid. 15:8). For the sexual organ - "and you, be fruitful and multiply" (Genesis 9:7), and it says (Jeremiah 29:6), "take wives, and beget [sons and daughters]." For the feet - "you shall walk in all the way which the LORD your God has commanded you" (Deuteronomy 5:30) - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:24: And so if he sinned in a sin that many stumbled in, he must merit the many through his deeds - and so they said in Tanna D'Vei Eliyahu, in the Yalkut, Parashat Ki Tisa, in the passage of the [golden] calf, in these words: Aaron knew himself that a great matter had come upon Israel through him, and he arose and tied an iron rope around his waist, and would go about all the camps of Israel - one who did not know [how to recite] the prayer, he taught him the prayer; one who did not know [how to recite] the Shema, he taught him the Shema; one not versed in the body of Torah, he brought him into the body of Torah. And not Aaron alone, but anyone who teaches Torah publicly to Israel for the sake of Heaven, the Omnipresent has mercy on him and grants him wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and intellect, and gives him his portion with the three righteous ones, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:25: And every penitent must teach the ways of repentance to whoever he knows has sinned, especially if it is a person accustomed to him and who will accept his words - as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 51:15), "I will teach transgressors Your ways." And concerning the virtue of one who brings the wicked back to repentance, several virtues are explained in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah, pages 128-129).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:26: Further, it is fitting to be careful of all aspects of theft - besides the theft of money, there is another theft, they said in Tractate Berachot (6b): Rav Chelbo said in the name of Rav Huna, whoever knows that his fellow is accustomed to greet him should be the one to greet him first, as it is said (Psalms 34:15), "seek peace and pursue it" - and if he greeted him and he did not return it, he is called a robber, as it is said (Isaiah 3:14), "and you, you have devoured the vineyard; the spoil of the poor is in your houses" - to this point. And Rashi, peace be upon him, explained "the spoil of the poor" - is not the spoil of the rich too, robbery? Rather, "the spoil of the poor" refers to one who has nothing else to rob from him except that his greeting is not returned.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:27: Further, he should be careful not to derive benefit from anything of the world without a blessing, for he is called a robber - as we say in Berachot (35b): Rabbi Chanina bar Papa said, whoever derives benefit from this world without a blessing is as though he robs the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Community of Israel, as it is said (Proverbs 28:24), "whoever robs his father or his mother, and says, it is no transgression, is a companion of a destroyer" - and "his father" is none other than the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said (Deuteronomy 32:6), "is He not your father who acquired you?" - and "his mother" is none other than the Community of Israel, as it is said (Proverbs 1:8), "hear, my son, the discipline of your father, and do not forsake the Torah of your mother." What is "a companion of a destroyer"? Rabbi Chanina bar Papa said, he is a companion of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who destroyed Israel from their Father in heaven - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:28: And Rashi, of blessed memory, explained: "robs the Holy One, blessed be He" - of His blessing; "and the Community of Israel" - for when they sin, the fruits are struck. "It is no transgression" - and because he treats it lightly, others see and learn from him to do the same, to benefit from this world without a blessing, and therefore this one who treats it lightly is called "a companion of a destroyer" - of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who sinned and caused others to sin; so he sins and causes others to sin - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:29: And above, in chapter 2, we explained that even one who does not occupy himself with Torah and commandments properly is called a robber - and especially in this exile of ours, when the Shechinah is exiled because of our iniquities, as he says (Isaiah 50:1), "and for your transgressions your mother was sent away" - and she has no rest or union except through us, when we occupy ourselves with Torah and commandments, and whoever does not occupy himself is called a robber. And they said in the Zohar, Parashat Vayeshev (page 191b): and whoever does not gaze at the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He, causes the Shechinah to be subdued into the dust, as it is said (Isaiah 26:5), "He shall bring it low, He shall lay it low, even to the ground," and so on. And so they said in Parashat Va'etchanan (page 268a), whose words we copied in the Gate of Love (chapter 8), that one who refrains from occupying himself with Torah is as though he withheld from the Shechinah her sustenance, clothing, and conjugal due.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:30: And behold, in exile she is called a widow, as he says (Lamentations 1:1), "she has become like a widow," and the righteous [Yesod] is an orphan - and for this the Torah commanded (Exodus 22:21), "you shall not afflict any widow or orphan" - and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Mechilta D'Rashbi), even a king's widow - and in exile she is the widow of the King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, as it were - and one must not delay her judgment [i.e., her redemption], and likewise perform the unifications relevant to the righteous, and not delay his judgment. For "if you shall afflict him at all" [doubled verb] - to indicate both the plain sense and the hidden meaning: the lower orphan and the lower widow, and the supernal allusion, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:31: Further, he should be careful of wronging [others], even wronging with words - and wronging with words is worse than wronging with money, as explained in Bava Metzia (58b), where it says there: three, the curtain [before the Divine Presence] is not locked before them, and these are: theft, wronging, and idolatry. Wronging, as it is written (Amos 7:7), "behold, the LORD stood upon a wall made by a plumb line, with a plumb line in His hand." Theft, as it is written (Jeremiah 6:7), "violence and plunder is heard in her before Me continually." Idolatry, as it is written (Isaiah 65:3), "a people who provoke Me to My face continually" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:32: Further, he should be careful of these four things, for one who does one of them is called wicked. They said in the Pesikta (Rabbati, Addition 1, parashah 4): three are called wicked - one who raises his hand against his fellow, as it is said (Exodus 2:13), "and he said to the wicked one, why do you strike your fellow?"; one who causes strife, as it is said (Numbers 16:26), "depart, please, from the tents of these wicked men"; and one who borrows and does not repay, as it is said (Psalms 37:21), "the wicked borrows, and does not repay." Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Tanchum said, Rabbi Tanchuma said to me, also one who is brazen-faced, as it is said (Proverbs 21:29), "a wicked man hardens his face" - to this point.
